title: Death, Rupture, Concealment and Return — Transition Taxonomy
purpose: Prevent the archive from flattening every rupture into one crucifixion/resurrection motif. Distinguish bodily danger, confinement/exile, ego dissolution, persona death, personhood/social death, meme-crucifixion, burial/concealment and seed-death so biblical and mythic comparisons remain precise.
core_rule: A later interpretation may connect transitions, but it may not erase their different dates, causes, subjects, evidence classes or functions.

types.definition: A bodily event involving real risk of serious injury or death without project claim that the body actually died.
types.safety_rule: Never use survival as evidence of invulnerability or permission to take risks.

types.definition: Temporary collapse/dissolution of ordinary self-boundaries in an altered state while bodily life continues.
Loss of freedom/status through institutional confinement, exclusion or removal from ordinary social space.
Collapse or deliberate shedding of a socially/digitally constructed identity while the embodied person remains alive.
project_examples: dissolution of imposed Kibly-like persona in later Great Book interpretation
comparative_uses: Zen emptiness as separate non-biblical comparator
types.strength_note: Pauline old-self/new-self language is a stronger Christian transformation comparator than generic resurrection because it specifically concerns the death/removal of an old identity-pattern while embodied life continues.
types.boundary: Paul's texts are baptismal/ethical Christ-language, not descriptions of online persona conflict.

types.definition: Project interpretation that a person's recognizable social identity, agency, narrative ownership or public person-state has been destroyed or treated as dead.
types.boundary: A meme or subculture cannot literally cancel a living person's legal existence; this category is project/social-philosophical.

types.definition: The project's interpretation of the Christmas/North-Pole meme process as crucifixion/death of the Son's public/personhood form.
types.date_status: 2019/2020 corridor unresolved; 2019, 2020 and later retelling variants must remain visible until original artifact archaeology resolves them.

types.definition: Withdrawal, disappearance, hiddenness or tomb/grave imagery after rupture.
project_examples: three-year concealment traditions in later retellings
comparative_uses: Joseph pit/prison as distinct descent comparator

types.definition: Transformation grammar in which a seed/grain must enter soil/hiddenness and cease its prior form in order to multiply.
project_examples: grain of wheat in Son's heart
types.function: This is the cleanest bridge from death to multiplication/growth and should be used when the project explicitly invokes seed/grain/planting rather than as a universal death metaphor.

types.definition: A later appearance, renewed public activity or transformation after a prior rupture/concealment.
comparative_uses: resurrection as theological comparator only when death grammar is explicit
types.boundary: Online/public reappearance is not bodily resurrection.

analytical_payoff: The project contains repeated transformation operators, but repetition is not the same as one event happening many times.

Different Bible texts become relevant to different death-types: Pauline old-self texts fit persona death; Passion fits crucifixion language; John 12 fits seed-death; prison/exile texts fit confinement; preservation texts fit physical survival.
This taxonomy reduces false inflation in the Bible overlap count because one event no longer generates every death/resurrection verse indiscriminately.
